newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rise in overnight rate due to seasonal demand--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Rise in overnight rate due to seasonal demand--BOJ.

text.p: Today's rise in the key overnight call rate was due to strong fund-raising demand by commercial banks ahead of the end of the month, a Bank of Japan (BOJ) official told Reuters on Thursday.
The official also said that the BOJ has been continuing its daily money market operations within the commitments the bank announced on September 8, 1995.

"The rise in the key overnight rate was attributed to several factors, including banks' preference for short-term funds and their seasonal fund demand ahead of the end of the fiscal year. But the major reason was banks' strong fund demand ahead of the end of the month," the official said.

The key overnight call rate briefly rose as high as 0.55 percent in the morning. But the rate was mainly traded at 0.53 percent by midday, traders said. Wednesday's weighted average rate was 0.51 percent.
Traders said the key overnight rate jumped this morning because the BOJ continued its neutral operations and paid little attention to banks' strong fund demand.
But the BOJ official said: "(The BOJ) has been conducting operations within the commitments it made in September 1995."

When the BOJ last cut its discount rate, to 0.50 percent from one percent on September 8, 1995, the bank said it expected the key overnight call rate to move slightly below the discount rate on average as it would make efforts to supply sufficient funds to the money market.
